Managing Partner

Shyam Sundar Pani

Shyam

Connecting businesses, relationships and opportunities for growth.

Shyam brings more than thirty years of experience in entrepreneurship, business growth, strategic communications and international partnerships, with an extensive network across businesses, industry associations and public institutions.

Emailshyam@setuhashi.com

LinkedIn profile ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Experience he brings

Shyam has advised business owners and leadership teams on market development, positioning and expansion. His work includes helping international businesses enter India and supporting Indian businesses pursuing opportunities in the United States and Europe.

His experience spans technology, advanced engineering, infrastructure, health and wellness. Alongside advisory work, he has founded and operated ventures, developed international relationships, and negotiated licensing and manufacturing arrangements with European partners.

He has also worked at the intersection of business and public institutions, helping organizations navigate stakeholder relationships, regulatory questions and the practical conditions for growth.

A connection rooted in India

Born and raised in India, Shyam brings a close understanding of its entrepreneurial environment, particularly Bengaluru’s business ecosystem, where he is based. He enjoys connecting people and organizations whose capabilities, ambitions and relationships can create possibilities together.

His commitment to SetuHashi

At SetuHashi, Shyam brings entrepreneurial energy, business relationships and practical knowledge of India. Working alongside Raju and Mak, he is committed to helping Japanese and Indian businesses recognize complementary strengths, build productive relationships and turn opportunities into business.

Selected experience

Examples from Shyam’s work before SetuHashi, and from individual advisory work with Mak. They are not work carried out by SetuHashi.

  • Building an Indian manufacturer’s international reputation

    Building visibility for an Indian manufacturer with prospective customers in Japan and the United States.

  • Helping overseas-backed technology start-ups build teams in India

    Supporting overseas-backed businesses as they built teams in India.

  • Concluding technology partnerships with Israeli and Korean companies

    Negotiating international technology partnerships to extend an Indian business’s portfolio.

  • Positioning a region for technology investment

    Positioning an Indian region to attract technology investment.

  • Negotiating an ownership transition for a software business

    Finding a buyer and negotiating terms for an Indian business’s ownership transition.

  • Developing two routes into Turkey

    Using business relationships to develop market-entry routes, and recognising when to pause.
